company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS with $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the quality was low — the beat was driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins. Domestic comps missed at +1.6% versus the expected +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year over year to 33.4% of sales. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final eight weeks and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex more aggressively in the fast-growing Physical AI and robotics perception space.

MillerKnoll reported solid FQ1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, implying an organic beat of 42 cents versus 36 cents expected. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million versus the $943.2 million consensus, though orders rose 3.5% year over year. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed to $3.88–4.03 billion from $3.93–4.13 billion, while the EPS range was held unchanged at $1.85–2.15.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings significant large-cap CFO experience, having previously served in that role at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The leadership change is seen as a routine transition rather than a strategic shift.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year over year to 12.4% versus the 13.85% expectation, despite revenue coming in slightly above consensus at $2.311 billion. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressures weighing on retail, while rising material costs pressured margins significantly. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost actions underway, and a roughly 75% year-over-year surge in the North American towable RV order backlog, though the company declined to provide formal fiscal 2027 guidance.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after the company reported positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. The result is a significant milestone for the company's obesity pipeline and positions VK2735 as a competitive asset in the crowded but high-growth GLP-1 space. The pre-market spike reflects strong investor enthusiasm for the data readout.

sectors: RV and recreational vehicle sector faces headwinds per THOR Industries commentary — stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressures are keeping retail soft and compressing margins. The robotics and machine vision space gets a strategic signal from Cognex's acquisition of RealSense, highlighting consolidation around Physical AI and depth-sensing technology.
tts_summary:
Here's your morning earnings rundown for Tuesday September 22nd. Six names reported before the open — let's go through them.

Starting with AutoZone. The company beat on fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share, coming in at $56.05 versus the Street at $54.03. But don't get too excited — this was a low-quality beat. A 145 basis point tailwind from tariff refunds and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins did the heavy lifting. Domestic comps missed, coming in at plus 1.6% versus the plus 3.1% expected, and operating expenses as a percent of sales rose 100 basis points year over year. Management did point to improving sales momentum in the back half of the quarter and said they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027 growth. Mixed picture overall.

Cognex is acquiring RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI — for roughly $500 million upfront plus another $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80 to $90 million in revenue, which is more than 50% year-over-year growth. This is a strategic move deeper into the Physical AI and robotics space. Bullish signal for Cognex.

MillerKnoll delivered a strong earnings beat — 53 cents versus the 36 cents expected. Importantly, even backing out the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, they still would have beaten at 42 cents. Sales missed at $923 million versus $943 million expected, though orders were up 3.5% year over year. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed slightly, but EPS guidance was held unchanged. Call it mixed with a lean toward positive on the earnings quality story.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st. He comes with serious pedigree, having been CFO at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox. Routine leadership transition, not a red flag.

THOR Industries missed. Fiscal fourth quarter earnings came in at 78 cents versus 87 cents expected. Gross margins fell 230 basis points year over year to 12.4%, well below the nearly 14% the Street had modeled. Management's tone was cautious — citing stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure keeping retail soft. No formal fiscal 2027 guidance yet. There were some offsets: dealer inventory is healthy, structural cost actions are underway, and the North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year over year. But the headline read is bearish.

Finally, Viking Therapeutics is the one to watch this morning. Shares are spiking pre-market after the company reported a 22% weight loss result from its GLP-1 drug VK2735 in clinical trials. That is a strong data readout and puts Viking firmly on the map as a credible competitor in the obesity drug space. Clearly bullish.

Bottom line for the session: Viking is the momentum play on positive trial data. AutoZone and MillerKnoll are mixed — beat the number but with asterisks. THOR is the clearest negative. Cognex's acquisition is strategically sound. Stay nimble.
